doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Technology, guitar synthesizer and amplifiers
summary: Technology mattered less than expected; he gave up the guitar synthesizer for the guitar's nuance.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How much has the changing technology allowed you or helped you to do some of that, to go in those different directions?

At one time I thought maybe it had a lot to do with it but I really don’t think it has too much to do with it. I think I’ve always enjoyed, even in a low tech world, to experiment and try to pull things out of the guitar that made it sound not so much like a guitar. I think the only period where it became even further removed from that was when things got more synthetic. I was fooling around with a guitar synthesizer when the guitar was attached to all sorts of keyboards and modules and then it really started to, I enjoyed it, but it started to get so far away from playing the guitar that, and I — and there was also a lot of problems involved and a lot of equipment, and just too much stuff, you can’t go on the road, you can’t travel with all this, so I just basically gave it all away and went back to playing the guitar. So I really think maybe that was one place where technology kind of came in and said oh, you have a lot more opportunities now. You don’t even have to sound like a guitar, you can sound like a flute or a piano. And that was, I went crazy with it. I thought it was just fantastic. But then after a while I just came back to the guitar. Because there was more nuance in it somehow. And there’s more control. You can do

more with the string, you know you can bend it and inflect it, but you can’t do that with a synthesizer as well. So I don’t think the technology has played that much of a role. I think things sound better now. In the old days you didn’t have much of a choice, you had like two different kinds of amplifiers to play through. Now you’ve got like a lot of different things you can choose from and digital reverberations and kind of things that make the music sound like it’s been recorded. So when you hear it live it has a more pleasant sound to my ears then just something that’s coming out of a broken, you know, Fender amp speaker. And in the old days, that’s pretty much all you had. You had like an amp and you were lucky if it was working.
